title: Best AI for sprite sheets
author: Electronic-Shine3271
selftext:
Hello AI Devs! So I've been using AI to make a game for a while now, and have run into the biggest road block yet...Art.

Now I know that without a doubt a artist that understand the vibe and design and understands how to make game art assets would be the absolute best choice, but I don't have money to invest and haven't come across an artist that wants to work for free!

That being said I've been trying different AI sprite sheet generators and was wanting some feedback. I've used [Spritesheet.ai](http://Spritesheet.ai), [https://gamelabstudio.co/](https://gamelabstudio.co/), and ludo. They all seem comparable, with each requiring money for credits.

I feel like I generated some decent sheets with gamelabstudio that I will link for reference but I didn't know what everyone suggest ESSPECIALLY if there is a similar option that is really free!

All the ones I've tested give you a couple credits to play with and then you have to pay after that, and as I mentioned I don't have the spare money to invest into this hobby!

Would love to know what yall are using! For context my game is a 2d Graphic Painterly Style (Not Pixel) you can see it here for reference! [https://github.com/ChaseKing77/threadbound](https://github.com/ChaseKing77/threadbound)

[Generated with Gamelabstudio! IF you want to try gamelabstudio use my ref code for free credits please! https:\/\/gamelabstudio.co\/?refcode=dyuatk34](https://reddit.com/link/1t4uu1c/video/mw90bjd3cezg1/player)

comments.author: Shadowlance23
comments.body:
You're unlikely to find any for free for the simple fact that these services have to pay their back end model provider.

You could probably bypass the middleman and just use the models directly on whatever free tier they provide. I've had some luck building sprite sheets in Gemini (Nano Banana 2 model). Not perfect, and I've got the pro subscription although I believe you get a few gens on the free tier with the original model. 

The results have been pretty good though. Only problem I've had so far is the sprites are misaligned, but a few minutes in [Paint.NET](http://Paint.NET) fixed that.

comments.body: How good of a GPU do you have? You might be able to run something locally.

replies.body: I think you can still do it, but it's better with Linux. I haven't done that though, so I can't exactly guide you through it.

comments.author: sumane12
comments.body: Image to AI video generator and extract the frames.

replies.author: Electronic-Shine3271
replies.body: What’s the workflow here? Can I use gpt for video and where would I extract?

replies.author: sumane12
replies.body:
Ask chatgpt what the workflow would be.

No chatgpt cannot generate video. You would need a video generator for that.

To extract the frames, load the video into a video editor and manually select each frame in the video to make your animation.
